subject: general
question: What will be the amount after 1 year if ₹9,900 is invested at 20% compound interest per annum, compounded half-yearly?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For **half-yearly** compounding at 20% **per annum**, the **half-yearly rate** is 10%.

Net **effective interest rate** for 2 half-years = 10 + 10 + (10 × 10) ÷ 100 = **21%**.

Total **Amount** = 121% of **Principal**.

Amount = 9900 × 1.21 = 11979.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹11,979.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹9,900

**Rate (R)** = 20% p.a.

**Time (T)** = 1 year

**Formula used:**

For **half-yearly compounding**, Rate (r) = R/2 and Time (n) = 2T

Amount (A) = P × (1 + r/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/32cf263c49383346284a4638486d22e7f9e86044d3ae065328a449e174c33e63.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Adjusted Rate (r) = 20 ÷ 2 = **10%** per half-year

⇒ Adjusted Time (n) = 1 × 2 = **2** half-years

⇒ A = 9900 × (1 + 10/100)²

⇒ A = 9900 × (11/10)²

⇒ A = 9900 × (121 ÷ 100)

⇒ A = 99 × 121

⇒ A = 11979

**∴ The correct answer is ₹11,979.**

**__Additional Information__**

Compounding Frequency Rules

When interest is compounded **quarterly**, the rate becomes R/4 and the time periods become 4T.

Compound Interest vs Simple Interest

For the **first conversion period**, SI and CI are equal. The difference for 2 periods is P(R/100)².

Effective Rate Formula

The **effective annual rate** (EAR) is given by (1 + r/n)ⁿ − 1, where n is the number of compounding periods.
